newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar may reach 1.80 dmk in 6 months - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Dollar may reach 1.80 dmk in 6 months - analyst.

text.p: The U.S. dollar is likely to strengthen to 1.80 marks in the coming six months and mere statements from policymakers on the dollar's level will not be sufficient to stem its rise, a senior German analyst said on Monday.

The fundamental factors driving the dollar higher against the mark are so strong that it will take concrete action in the form of currency market intervention to weaken the U.S. unit, Juergen Graf, chief analyst at Frankfurt-based SGZ-Bank, told Reuters at a conference on exchange rates here.
"Statements alone cannot lower the dollar. If there is no concrete intervention I cannot imagine that one can weaken the dollar significantly," Graf said.
Graf said he could imagine central banks will start to enter currency markets to intervene if the dollar hits a level of 1.76 marks or 1.77 marks.
He said the dollar was being driven by the fact that U.S. short-term and long-term interest rates were higher than Germany's and by uncertainty about the launch of Europe's planned single currency.

Graf said this morning's rise in the dollar against the mark and the yen were explained by the covering of short positions on the dollar after Sunday's meeting of policymakers of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations.
The G7 issued what currency dealers regarded as a benign statement on currencies after the meeting.
It said major foreign exchange misalignments had been corrected, that excessive volatility was undesirable and that there was a need to avoid currency moves that could lead to unbalanced trade.

But the statement did not make any explicit reference to dollar strength or yen weakness, nor did it suggest that active intervention from German, Japanese or U.S. central banks was imminent, traders and analysts said.
Currency traders reacted by pushing the dollar to a three-year high against the mark of 1.7389, and above 127 yen, just shy of a four-and-a-half year peak of 127.19 touched earlier this month.
